title: See every running session
outcome: Every tmux session on your computer appears as a row with its program, folder and whether it is working, waiting or done.
where: Session list (home screen on a phone; the sidebar on a laptop)

agent.text: Read the list with the pairing token to see every session's title, cwd and watcher state (active, waiting, ready, idle). It is read-only: nothing changes on the user's device.

title: See what each session is doing
outcome: A session's row shows the program's own window title, such as an agent's current task.
where: Automatic

agent.text: Set your pane title with an OSC 2 (or OSC 0) escape, e.g. printf '\033]2;%s\033\\' 'Refactoring auth'; the row shows it on the next list refresh with leading symbols stripped. A title shaped like user@host: /path, or equal to the hostname, is ignored and the row shows the folder name instead.

title: Refresh the session list
outcome: Pull the list down, or press reload, to fetch the latest sessions and their states.
where: Pull down on the session list, or the reload button in its header

title: Start a new session
outcome: Create a fresh terminal session on your computer and open it; leave the name blank and one is made up for you.
where: Session list > + New session

agent.text: Creates a detached tmux session (name required, max 60 chars, no '.' or ':'; dir defaults to ~). It appears in the user's list on the next refresh but does not open on their screen; the sess-MMDD-HHMM default name is the app's, not the route's.

title: New session from the keyboard
outcome: One key press creates a session with a default name and opens it, without the naming dialog.
where: Ctrl+Shift+L

title: Jump to a session by number
outcome: Switch straight to the first to ninth session in the sidebar with one key combination.
where: Ctrl+Shift+1 to 9

title: Rename a session
outcome: Give a session a display name every device shows, or change its real tmux name.
where: Pencil icon on a session row > Display name / tmux name > Save

agent.text: Sets the display name every device shows without renaming the session (an empty alias clears it), same as tmux set-option -t <session> @alias '<text>'. POST /api/session/rename {session, name} instead changes the real tmux name and drops every device's view of it, so use that only when asked.

title: Close a session
outcome: End a session after a confirmation, on every device that has it open.
where: Trash icon on a session row, or Kill in the rename sheet

agent.text: Only on the user's explicit request: kills the session and every device view grouped onto it, with no undo. A plain tmux kill-session on the base session would leave the device views alive.

title: Use one session from several devices
outcome: A phone, tablet and laptop can watch one session at once, each at its own screen size.
where: Automatic

agent.text: Sessions named <device>-<session> (or <device>-<session>-2..9, or ptui-<session>) grouped onto a user's session are PocketTUI's per-device views; tmux ls lists them as grouped. Do not attach to, rename or kill them: they are recreated on every connect and swept when stale.

title: Pick up after a dropped connection
outcome: When the phone sleeps or the network drops, reopening the app returns you to the same screen without a redraw or lost terminal modes.
where: Automatic

title: Each session keeps its side panes
outcome: Files, browser tabs or changes open beside a session come back when you return to it.
where: Automatic (switch sessions in the sidebar)

title: Search the whole terminal history
outcome: Find text anywhere in a session's scrollback, step between matches and see them highlighted in the terminal.
where: Ctrl+Shift+F

where: Message box under the terminal (always shown on touch; the mic key toggles it on a laptop) > Send

agent.text: Text the user sends from the box arrives in your pane as one bracketed paste followed by Enter, so a multi-line message is a single submission, never line by line.

group: Type and talk from a phone

agent.text: An attached file is saved as ~/.pockettui/uploads/<name>-<stamp>-<hex>.<ext> (newest 30 kept) and its absolute path is typed into the user's message; images go through the image-paste path instead.

title: Install speech engines on the computer
outcome: Download the Parakeet or Whisper speech engine onto your computer so dictation runs there.
where: On the computer: ./setup_voice.sh (or the voice question the installer asks)

agent.text: Run bash ~/pockettui/setup_voice.sh --parakeet, --whisper or --all (no prompts; piped with no flag it installs both). Nothing leaves the machine; the phone's Settings > Dictation rows turn available once /api/voice_status reports the engine.

title: Browse your computer's files
outcome: Browse your computer's folders, starting at home or at the folder your terminal is in.
where: Folder button on the session list (home), or the folder key in the key bar (session's folder)

title: Tap printed file paths
outcome: Paths printed in the terminal become links that open the file or folder in the right viewer.
where: Tap or click a path printed in the terminal

agent.text: Print absolute or ~/ paths (e.g. /home/u/out/report.md) and the user can tap them; printing does not open anything. The path must start at line start or after whitespace, a quote, ( [ { < = : or a comma, and stops at whitespace, quotes, brackets, : ; , so file.py:42 links only file.py; wrapped lines are stitched back together.

title: View printed images and videos
outcome: When the terminal prints the path of a picture or video, tapping it opens it full-screen with no copying step.
where: Tap or click a printed .png/.jpg/.gif/.webp/.svg/.bmp/.mp4/.webm/.mov path

agent.text: Print the absolute path of an image or video you produced (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, svg, bmp, mp4, webm, mov); the user taps it to view it full-screen. A printed .pdf path opens the PDF view, .md the rendered reader, .html a sandboxed page in a new tab, and anything else the editor.

title: Zoom into pictures and videos
outcome: Images and videos open in a viewer with pinch and double-tap zoom, panning and download.
where: Tap an image or video in the file browser or terminal; pinch, drag or double-tap inside the viewer

title: Read PDFs
outcome: PDFs open beside the terminal on a laptop and in a new browser tab on a phone.
where: Tap a .pdf in the file browser or terminal

title: File browser follows the terminal
outcome: The docked file browser keeps showing whatever folder the terminal beside it has moved into.
where: Automatic (docked file browser still on the terminal's folder)

agent.text: The pane follows tmux's pane_current_path, which is the cwd of the pane's foreground process: a cd typed at the shell moves it, but a cd inside an agent's own subprocess does not. Print the folder's absolute path instead so the user can tap it.

title: Follow a folder over ssh
outcome: When the terminal is logged into another machine over ssh, the file browser opens the same folder if your computer mounts it too.
where: Automatic (docked file browser, ssh pane)

agent.text: Only for a pane whose foreground command is ssh: the remote shell must set its title to user@host: /absolute/path before any TUI takes over (tmux keeps the last such title in the pane option @ptui_remote_cwd). The path is used only if it exists locally, directly or through POCKETTUI_PATH_REWRITES; ~ paths are refused.

title: List or grid, sorted your way
outcome: Show files as a list or a grid of icons, sorted by name, newest, oldest or size.
where: File browser > layout pop-up (grid glyph)

title: Picture previews in the grid
outcome: In grid view, images, videos and PDFs show a small preview instead of a generic icon.
where: Automatic in grid view

where: File browser > branch pop-up at the right of the path bar (inside a repo)

where: File browser > edit-path button beside the path bar

where: File browser > + > New file / New folder

outcome: Delete a file or an empty folder after confirming.
where: Long-press (or right-click) a file > Delete

where: File browser > + > Upload

outcome: Drop a folder on the file browser, or pick one, and it lands in the folder on screen with its subfolders, asking once before replacing files already there.
where: Drag a folder onto the file list, or File browser > + > Upload folder

outcome: Drag a file onto a folder, tile or breadcrumb to move it, even between two file browsers.
where: Drag a row onto a folder, tile or breadcrumb

outcome: Save a file from your computer onto the device in your hand.
where: Long-press a file > Download, or the download icon in the editor, reader or viewer

outcome: Download a folder as one zip file, built as it downloads.

where: Tap a text file in the file browser, or Edit in its action sheet

agent.text: If you write a file the user has open in the editor, their next Save gets a conflict prompt (Overwrite or Reload) instead of silently replacing your change; nothing is shown to them until they press Save.

agent.text: Write a .md file (tables, task lists, $...$ and $$...$$ maths, images by relative path) and print its absolute path; the user taps it and reads it rendered. The file's content can never run script in the reader.

agent.text: The pane lists the repository that contains the session pane's cwd, so edits you make there show up for the user to stage or revert per block; it refreshes by polling, you do not need to signal it.

agent.text: Print http://localhost:PORT (or 127.0.0.1 / 0.0.0.0) for a server listening on loopback. On tap the phone rewrites the host to the computer's address and asks the backend (POST /api/relay {host, port}) to relay that port number to your loopback listener; printing alone opens and binds nothing, and nothing is relayed until the server is actually listening.

agent.text: The code lives in ~/pockettui/.token (mode 0600, readable by the user the service runs as). Send it as the X-PocketTUI-Token header on /api/* calls; never print it into the terminal, since every device attached to the session would see it.

agent.text: Run pockettui update on the computer (--allow-downgrade to go back). The service restarts but tmux sessions survive; from the app the same update runs in a tmux session named pockettui-update, and GET /api/update_status reports {state, session_alive}.

agent.text: Types literal text at the prompt of a named session's active pane; every \r and \n is stripped so it never runs, and the user must press Enter. Use it to stage a command for the user in another session (max 4096 chars); it does not create a session and does not switch the user's screen.

title: Manage PocketTUI from the command line
outcome: A pockettui command on the computer updates, reports status and version, and installs the browser.
where: On the computer: pockettui update | version | status | browser

agent.text: Commands: pockettui update [--allow-downgrade], pockettui version, pockettui status, pockettui browser install|check|status. Installed at ~/.local/bin/pockettui; none of them touch the user's device directly.

title: Keeps running in the background
outcome: PocketTUI runs as a background service that restarts on its own, and updates restart it without closing your sessions.
where: Automatic (installer offers to set it up)

agent.text: Linux: systemctl --user status pockettui and journalctl --user -u pockettui; macOS: the launchd agent logs to ~/pockettui/pockettui.log. Restarting the service keeps tmux sessions alive (KillMode=process).

title: See which session needs you
outcome: Each session shows whether it is working, waiting for an answer, ready for your next message, or idle.
where: Automatic (badge on each session row)

agent.text: State is read from your pane after output stops for 6 s: a y/n or yes/no question, 'do you want / would you like / proceed? / continue? / are you sure', two or more numbered options (1. 2.), or one ❯-marked choice over another line reads as waiting; an empty ❯ or > composer reads as ready; anything else is idle. There is no route to set it; end a question with a clear '(y/n)' or a numbered list and then stop printing.

title: Answer a prompt with one tap
outcome: When a program asks yes/no or offers numbered choices, buttons for each answer appear above the keys.
where: Automatic chips row above the terminal; tap a chip

agent.text: A detected y/n question gets y and n chips, a numbered menu gets its first four digits, and an unnumbered chooser or trailing question gets only Enter and Esc (always added). A tap sends just that key to your pane, with no Enter after a digit or letter; the chips go away as soon as the pane prints again.

title: Unread marks on sessions
outcome: A session that starts waiting while you are looking elsewhere keeps a dot until you open it.
where: Automatic (dot on the session row)

title: Get notified by a session
outcome: Turn on sound or silent alerts per session, so your phone tells you when it needs input or finishes.
where: Bell icon on a session row (cycles off, sound, silent)

agent.text: This only stores the session's notification preference (tmux option @notify: off, on or quiet), like tmux set-option -t <session> @notify on; it sends nothing. Change it only when the user asks.

title: Alerts on a locked phone
outcome: Alerts reach your phone with the app closed when a session asks a question, finishes or rings the bell.
where: Turning on the first session's bell asks for permission

agent.text: A push fires only for sessions whose @notify is on or quiet, at most once per 30 s per session: when a question is detected, when an agent returns to an empty composer after at least 30 s of work, when a command of 10 s or more finishes back at the shell, or at once when the pane rings the terminal bell (printf '\a', subject to tmux flagging the bell). No route sends one.

title: Send alerts to ntfy
outcome: Notifications can also go to an ntfy topic, for phones where browser push is not available.
where: On the computer: set POCKETTUI_NTFY_URL in the service environment

agent.text: Set POCKETTUI_NTFY_URL (and optionally POCKETTUI_APP_URL for the tap-through link) in the service's environment and restart it; the same notifications as push go to that topic, lower priority in quiet mode.

title: Alerts open the right session
outcome: Tapping a notification opens the app straight on the session it was about, even if the phone had closed the app.
where: Tap a push or ntfy notification

title: iPhone alerts need Home Screen
outcome: On an iPhone browser tab, turning on alerts explains that the app must be added to the Home Screen first.
where: Automatic message on the first bell tap

title: Light, dark or automatic
outcome: Choose a light or dark look for the whole app, or follow your device's setting.
where: Theme button in the header, or Settings > Appearance > App theme

title: Pick terminal colour schemes
outcome: Pick one of twelve colour schemes for light mode and one for dark; the whole app follows them.
where: Settings > Appearance > Terminal palette (and Reset)

title: Import your own colour scheme
outcome: Paste or upload a scheme from iTerm2, Windows Terminal or xterm, and remove it later if you want.
where: Settings > Appearance > Paste a scheme / Choose file > Use scheme; x beside Custom to remove

title: Readable colours on any theme
outcome: Text colours are adjusted so every character stays readable against its background, even on a light theme.
where: Automatic

title: Change text size with buttons
outcome: Plus and minus buttons set the terminal's text size and the sidebar's separately.
where: Settings > Keys > Text size

title: Add an Alt key
outcome: Put an Alt key on the phone's key bar for programs that need it.
where: Settings > Keys > Alt key

title: See every keyboard shortcut
outcome: A list of every shortcut the app understands, with a short version in the sidebar.
where: Settings > Keys, or the Shortcuts card in the sidebar

title: Edit with Vim keys
outcome: Turn on Vim keys in the editor; your .vimrc settings and mappings apply, and :w, :q, :wq work.
where: Editor > Vim

agent.text: The editor reads ~/.vimrc when Vim mode is switched on and applies the set options and map/noremap lines it can translate; edits you make to ~/.vimrc apply the next time the user turns Vim mode on (plugins and functions are skipped).

title: Your terminal stays between your devices
outcome: Your device talks straight to your computer; sessions, keystrokes and files never pass through PocketTUI's servers.
where: Automatic

title: App adapts to older servers
outcome: The app asks the computer what it supports and only shows buttons that will work there.
where: Automatic

agent.text: Read the capability map to learn which features this server has (a missing or false flag means absent): fs, image_paste, upload, voice, learned, push, dbg, git, git_ref, search, ping, update, pair_qr, update_status, type, relay, browse, browse_tab, bookmarks, zip_dir, thumbs, browser_full, pdf_thumbs, upload_dirs. It is frozen at server start.

title: Check a PocketTUI server answers
outcome: A public check tells the app, or a script, whether PocketTUI is running at an address and which version.
where: Automatic when the code fails or nothing answers

agent.text: No token needed; answers only product and version, no hostname, paths or capabilities. Use it to confirm the local backend (default http://127.0.0.1:5560) is up before an authenticated call.

title: On-screen debug log
outcome: Show the app's internal log on screen, like a browser console on a phone.
where: Settings > About > Debug log

title: Device logs reach the computer
outcome: While the debug log is on, the device's log lines are also written to the computer's server log.
where: Automatic while Settings > About > Debug log is on

agent.text: Read them as lines 'dbg[<device>] <text>' in journalctl --user -u pockettui (Linux) or ~/pockettui/pockettui.log (macOS); nothing is stored elsewhere and nothing arrives unless the user has switched Debug log on.

title: Notification taps in the debug log
outcome: With debug on, the last twenty notification taps are written to the debug log to diagnose alerts that open the wrong place.
where: Automatic at start-up when Debug log is on

title: Report a problem
outcome: Send a bug report with optional diagnostics straight to the PocketTUI team, even when your computer is unreachable.
where: Settings > About > Report a problem, or the report key in the laptop key pill

title: See diagnostics before sending
outcome: The report shows exactly which device details it would send, and you can leave them out.
where: Report sheet > include diagnostics

title: What PocketTUI is
outcome: A short description, privacy statement and links to the website, source code and support email.
where: Settings > About

title: Try it without a computer
outcome: A pretend terminal lets you try the app before installing anything.
where: Try demo on the session list when unpaired, or pockettui.com/demo

title: Install as a home-screen app
outcome: Add the app to your home screen to run it full-screen like a native app.
where: Share > Add to Home Screen (iPhone) or Menu > Install app (Android); reminder on setup step 2

title: Use the app without pockettui.com
outcome: Your computer serves its own copy of the app, and you can build a single HTML file with your address built in.
where: Open http://<computer>:5560/ directly, or run build_mobile.py --backend URL

title: Smooth terminal drawing
outcome: The terminal uses graphics acceleration for smooth scrolling and falls back quietly when it is unavailable.
where: Automatic

title: Keep recordings for testing
outcome: An operator setting keeps the latest voice recordings on the computer to test dictation accuracy; off by default.
where: On the computer: POCKETTUI_VOICE_KEEP=<n> in the service environment

agent.text: With POCKETTUI_VOICE_KEEP=<n> set, the newest n takes are kept in ~/pockettui/.voice_takes/<stem>.{orig,wav,json}; nothing in the app reads them back.
